lines.trans: Hey there. Are you the new guy?
Yeah. I am Max.
That is Fedya.
They played the exact same prank on me when I started.
Reporting for duty.
Viktor Petrovich.
I have good news for you.
Your MRI results just came back.
You simply cannot take your eyes off them.
Does that mean I can go back to work?
You will have to forget about work for at least two months.
What do you mean, for two months?
Two weeks here with us, and then bed rest at home.

meanings.note: Casual yes. Core Russian interj meaning 'uh-huh, yeah' in everyday speech.
Said ironically. Core Russian interj meaning 'uh-huh, yeah' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Yeah, right, like with the Cayenne?

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: 'закрывать глаза на' + accusative = to turn a blind eye to

examples.text: Я не буду закрывать на это глаза.
examples.trans: I'm not going to close my eyes to this.

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: House arrest. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('home, domestic').
House arrest. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('home, domestic').
Homework. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('home, domestic').

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: colloquial; stressed on the first syllable
Parenthetical. Core Russian adv meaning 'so, then, that means' in everyday speech.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?
что это значит? = what does this mean?
the form значит is used as a linking word

examples.trans: Pasha, what does all this mean?

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Уже месяц = for a month now. Common masculine noun meaning 'month' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I've been living here for a month.
The election is in a month.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.
The fish is at least three days old.

examples.text: Значит, этой рыбе минимум три дня.
examples.trans: That means this fish is at least three days old.

meanings.note: Asking permission. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
неделю = for a week; через неделю = in a week

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('newcomer').

examples.text: А вот это у нас новенький.
examples.trans: And this one here is our newcomer.
Hey there. Are you the new guy?

meanings.note: Plural, also the TV news programme. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'piece of news' in everyday Russian.

Plural, also the TV news programme. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'piece of news' in everyday Russian.
+ prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.en: to tear off, to rip off
meanings.note: Idiom. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to tear off', paired with 'отрывать'.
Idiom. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to tear off', paired with 'отрывать'.

examples.trans: Mum will tear my head off.

examples.text: Какая тебе опергруппа? Мне твоя мать голову оторвёт.
examples.trans: What field team? Your mother will tear my head off.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'быть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'arrive, increase'.

examples.text: Лицо ресторана прибыло, я готов встречать гостей!
examples.trans: The face of the restaurant arrived, I am ready to welcome guests!

examples.text: Главный гость уже прибыл, мы готовы подавать закуски!
examples.trans: The main guest has already arrived, we are ready to serve the appetizers!

examples.text: Поезд из Воронежа должен прибыть на вокзал ровно в девять утра.
examples.trans: The train from Voronezh is due to arrive at the station at nine in the morning sharp.

meanings.note: On foot, once. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.en: to have to, to be forced to
meanings.note: impersonal with dative: мне придётся = I'll have to

examples.trans: I'm going to have to torture you.
We had to wait a long time.

examples.text: Ты что, очкарик, не понимаешь? Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'undergoing, passing' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое прохождение.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new undergoing.

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Inanimate masculine noun. Common masculine noun meaning 'regime, routine, mode' in everyday Russian.
Common masculine noun meaning 'regime, routine, mode' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There is a strict hospital regime here.

examples.text: Здесь строгий режим и нельзя громко шуметь.
examples.trans: There is a strict regime here and one cannot make loud noise.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'result' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас.
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you.
This is an excellent result of the work.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас. Работайте!
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you. Get to work!

meanings.note: Literally 'until the meeting'. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.
Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.
Дорожная служба = road service. Common feminine noun meaning 'service, department' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'service, department' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Дорожная служба обещала закатать её десять лет назад.
examples.trans: The road service promised to pave it over ten years ago.
Right now we need to call social services.

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Classical Greek compound borrowing ('томография'), feminine noun. Common feminine noun meaning 'MRI scan' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая томография.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new MRI scan.
Let us wait for the MRI results.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Possession. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to joke', paired with 'пошутить'.

examples.text: Шутишь? Правда, скажи, где деньги? Меня наняли.
examples.trans: Are you joking? Seriously, tell me, where's the money? They hired me.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
